prompt_refinement.style_rules: Match the palette, brush feel, lighting, icon density, and framing discipline of the selected target's reference image. Keep the final subject and asset meaning driven by the selected batch entry, not the reference subject.
prompt_refinement.composition_rules: Use the reference only as a style guide. Keep the result in the same visual family, but make it visibly distinct at a glance by changing the silhouette, crop, object arrangement, and ornament placement. Do not mirror the reference composition or reuse its exact outline.

victory_tree_backgrounds.tree_rules: Create a clean 16:9 game background plate shot like a single photograph with real shallow depth of field, not a layered 2D illustration. Compose it as though a camera stands at ground level looking outward across a distant landscape, and a large tree standing near the camera happens to block most of the view. The tree is in crisp focus and fills most of the frame; the landscape behind it is the same continuous scene, just thrown out of focus by the lens (soft bokeh, reduced contrast and saturation, atmospheric haze with distance) rather than a flat blurred backdrop pasted behind a cutout — light direction, color temperature, and haze density must match between the tree and the background so they read as one photographed space. The tree must feel bigger than the frame: it enters from its specified edge already mid-structure, as if the camera simply couldn't fit the rest of it, so no root, base, or ground line should be visible or implied at that edge — the trunk or a branch is simply cropped by the frame there. From that cropped entry point, one continuous trunk line runs through five widely spaced main waypoints (natural bends or forks in the wood, not marked in any way), with exactly five side branches following only the listed connections, each reading as an ordinary uninterrupted stretch of branch. Keep branch corridors visually separated with no crossings or accidental extra branches, and keep a reasonable, uncluttered length of clear trunk/branch surface around each waypoint so a future circular UI element can be overlaid there later — but do not render any circle, ring, halo, glow, button, badge, medallion, dot, gem, endpoint marker, label, or icon anywhere on the tree. No text, letters, numbers, logos, UI frame, watermark, or readable map labels.

paths.label: Conquest Victory
paths.tree_prompt: Art direction: medieval illuminated-manuscript art rendered as a single photographed scene with real depth of field, distinctly different from the other routes; crimson red, aged parchment, black iron, muted bronze, and restrained gold leaf, with matching haze and light between the two depths. Background: a distant frontier war-camp valley, hazy stone fortress walls, and indistinct banners, softly out of focus behind the tree, same light and color grade as the foreground. Foreground: a crisp, severe heraldic ironwood tree standing close to the camera, its trunk like a campaign road and its branches disciplined and angular. Frame it so the trunk is cropped by the lower-left border, as if the camera only caught the upper reach of a much larger tree growing out of frame there — no root or ground line visible at that edge. From that cropped entry the trunk climbs diagonally across nearly the full frame toward the upper-right, passing through five widely spaced main waypoints (plain unmarked bends in the wood). Branch topology, not visible labels: B1 and B2 leave M1; B1 has two further bends and B2 has three. B3 and B4 leave M2; B3 has two further bends and B4 has three. B5 leaves M3 and has two further bends. Fan paired branches above and below the diagonal trunk, keep an uncluttered stretch of bark around every waypoint, and make the ascent feel forceful, territorial, and irreversible. Do not depict soldiers, weapons, shields, flags, or any circular marker on the tree.

paths.label: Prosperity Victory
paths.tree_prompt: Art direction: refined Art Nouveau botanical poster art rendered as a single photographed scene with real depth of field, distinctly different from the other routes; leaf green, warm cream, verdigris, harvest gold, and soft terracotta accents, with matching haze and light between the two depths. Background: a distant prosperous valley with orchards, a granary silhouette, terraces, roofs, and a far river, softly out of focus behind the tree, same light and color grade as the foreground. Foreground: an elegant cultivated living tree close to the camera, made of graceful stems, grain-like leaves, and subtle architectural latticework, crisp against the soft backdrop. Frame it so the trunk is cropped by the bottom-center border, as if the camera only caught the upper reach of a much larger tree growing out of frame there — no root or ground line visible at that edge. From that cropped entry the trunk rises vertically through most of the canvas toward the top-center, passing through five widely spaced main waypoints (plain unmarked bends in the stem). Branch topology, not visible labels: B1 and B2 leave M1; B1 has three further bends and B2 has four. B3 and B4 leave M2; B3 has two further bends and B4 has three. B5 leaves M3 and has three further bends. Keep B5 as a separate open branch, never looping back into an earlier branch. Fan the branches rhythmically left and right like irrigation channels and fruiting boughs, with an uncluttered stretch of stem around every waypoint. Do not use fruit, coins, buildings, harvest bundles, or any circular marker on the tree.

paths.label: Trade Victory
paths.tree_prompt: Art direction: carved maritime woodblock and antique portolan-chart print rendered as a single photographed scene with real depth of field, distinctly different from the other routes; gold yellow, ink navy, weathered teal, warm paper, and small copper accents, with matching haze and light between the two depths. Background: a distant harbor, sea lanes, sails, and warehouses, softly out of focus behind the tree, same light and color grade as the foreground. Foreground: one crisp braided trade-route tree close to the camera, made from a gold-and-ink grained trunk that runs strongly horizontal, with branches behaving like clean shipping corridors rather than literal roots. Frame it so the trunk is cropped by the left-center border, as if the camera only caught a stretch of a much larger tree extending out of frame there — no root or ground line visible at that edge. From that cropped entry the trunk travels across almost the entire canvas toward the right-center, passing through five widely spaced main waypoints (plain unmarked bends in the wood). Branch topology, not visible labels: B1 leaves M1 and has two further bends. B2 and B3 leave M2; B2 has three further bends and B3 has four. B4 and B5 leave M3; each has two further bends. Fan branch corridors above and below the horizontal trunk without crossings, keep an uncluttered stretch of wood around every waypoint, and make the route feel like expanding commercial reach. Do not draw ships, scales, coins, seals, compass points, port symbols, or any circular marker on the tree.

paths.label: Diplomatic Victory
paths.tree_prompt: Art direction: restrained Baroque copperplate engraving with diplomatic parchment flourishes rendered as a single photographed scene with real depth of field, distinctly different from the other routes; ivory white, pearl gray, ink black, muted lapis, and soft antique gold, with matching haze and light between the two depths. Background: a distant palace reception hall, embassy garden, and soft candlelit architecture, softly out of focus behind the tree, same light and color grade as the foreground. Foreground: a crisp, graceful tree of interwoven treaty ribbons and fine engraved filigree close to the camera, with a single unbroken trunk and clean, deliberate branch spacing. Frame it so the trunk is cropped by the upper-left border, as if the camera only caught a stretch of a much larger tree extending out of frame there — no root or ground line visible at that edge. From that cropped entry the trunk descends diagonally across nearly the full frame toward the lower-right, passing through five widely spaced main waypoints (plain unmarked bends in the ribbon-wood). Branch topology, not visible labels: B1 and B2 leave M1; B1 has two further bends and B2 has three. B3 and B4 leave M2; each has three further bends. B5 leaves M3 and has two further bends. Pair the branches in balanced opposing arcs around the diagonal, keep an uncluttered stretch of branch around every waypoint, and evoke negotiated connection rather than military force. Do not depict seals, rings, hands, doves, scroll ends, crowns, or any circular marker on the tree.

paths.label: Cultural Victory
paths.tree_prompt: Art direction: Chinese ink-wash painting on rice paper, composed like a single photographed vista with real atmospheric depth rather than a flat scroll layout, distinctly different from the other routes; charcoal black ink, soft royal-purple mineral pigment, faded indigo wash, and sparse warm paper tone, with matching mist density and tone between the two depths. Background: a distant misty wash suggesting academy roofs, theatre eaves, and mountain-cloud atmosphere, softly out of focus behind the tree, same wash tone as the foreground. Foreground: one commanding calligraphic ink tree close to the viewer, rendered with decisive dry-brush trunk strokes and restrained purple accents; it must remain clean enough for UI use, not a dense landscape painting. Frame it so the trunk is cropped by the lower-right border, as if the brush only captured the upper reach of a much larger tree extending out of frame there — no root or ground line visible at that edge. From that cropped entry the trunk rises diagonally across nearly the full frame toward the upper-left, passing through five widely spaced main waypoints (plain unmarked bends in the brushwork). Branch topology, not visible labels: B1 and B2 leave M1; each has two further bends. B3 and B4 leave M2; each has two further bends. B5 leaves M3 and has two further bends. Use flowing but unambiguous brush branches with broad blank-paper breathing room around every waypoint. Do not paint plum blossoms, masks, lyres, scroll seals, stars, ink splatters, or any circular marker on the tree, and do not add any Chinese characters.

paths.label: Scientific Victory
paths.tree_prompt: Art direction: clean contemporary modern technical graphic art rendered as a single photographed scene with real depth of field, distinctly different from the other routes; azure blue, cyan, cool white, graphite, and a restrained brass highlight, with matching haze and light between the two depths. Background: a distant field of observatory machinery, laboratory glass, and celestial arcs, softly out of focus behind the tree, same light and color grade as the foreground. Foreground: a crisp modern innovation tree close to the camera, made of a single luminous geometric spine with precise but organic circuit-like branch corridors; it is a reward tree, not a literal user interface. Frame it so the trunk is cropped by the top-center border, as if the camera only caught the lower reach of a much larger tree extending out of frame there — no root or ground line visible at that edge. From that cropped entry the trunk travels vertically down through most of the canvas toward the bottom-center, passing through five widely spaced main waypoints (plain unmarked bends in the spine). Branch topology, not visible labels: B1 and B2 leave M1; B1 has two further bends and B2 has three. B3 and B4 leave M2; each has two further bends. B5 leaves M3 and has two further bends. Fan branches alternately left and right, keep an uncluttered stretch of spine around every waypoint, no crossings, and a feeling of measured discovery progressing downward. Do not draw atoms, astrolabes, lenses, constellations, circuit pads, data dots, charts, glowing rings, or any circular marker on the tree.
